Künstler:innen  ·  Represented Artists

Twelve
artists

Beton Galerie represents twelve international artists working across sculpture, painting, video, installation, performance, sound, and photography. The gallery also collaborates with a small number of guest and past artists.

Medium
Generation

Solveig Tarkamp

b. 1981 Tromsø (NO) · lives Oslo & Berlin

Tarkamp works in polished basalt, salt, and projected light, drawing on extended residencies in arctic landscapes. Her practice unfolds over long durations and is grounded in collaboration with a single basalt quarry in Brandenburg.

View current solo →

Ade Okonkwo

b. 1978 Lagos (NG) · lives Berlin

Okonkwo makes video and sound installations that work with broadcast archives, oral history, and the long political life of radio. He collaborates frequently with archivists and composers.

View work →

Inés Berruga

b. 1975 Madrid (ES) · lives Madrid & Berlin

Berruga's paintings on raw linen use mineral pigments and a slow horizontal pull. Her recent work draws on landscapes of central Spain and the long history of European mark-making on cloth.

View work →

Hannes Reiter

b. 1969 Vienna (AT) · lives Vienna

Reiter works in wax, bronze, and oak. His Vorläufig series — small "provisional" figures intended to remain unfinished — has been ongoing since 2009.

View work →

Yui Maekawa

b. 1987 Kyoto (JP) · lives Berlin

Maekawa makes wall-mounted works in dyed silk and brass thread, combining Kyoto dyeing traditions with the long European tradition of the panel painting. Her work is held quiet and severe.

View work →

Khalid Saleh

b. 1972 Cairo (EG) · lives Cairo & Berlin

Saleh works with mud-brick architecture as sculpture. His installations are built on site by hand over weeks, and refer to vernacular construction traditions of the Western Desert and the Nile delta.

View work →

Margit Eilers

b. 1958 Düsseldorf (DE) · lives Berlin

Eilers is one of the gallery's first represented artists. She has made long horizontal pencil drawings for more than four decades, sustaining a single, unwavering line of inquiry.

View work →

Pieter van Aalst

b. 1984 Rotterdam (NL) · lives Rotterdam

Van Aalst's sound installations use disused European radio infrastructure, magnetic tape, and contact microphones. He has presented work at the Kunsthalle Wien and the Sonic Acts festival.

View work →

Léonie Charpentier

b. 1982 Lyon (FR) · lives Paris

Charpentier works between drawing, paper modelling, and built architectural fragments at room scale. Her practice has roots in her early training at the École nationale supérieure d'architecture de Paris-Belleville.

View work →

Daniela Cruz

b. 1980 São Paulo (BR) · lives Berlin

Cruz makes long-duration performance and installation works that often involve written scores enacted by the artist alone or with a small ensemble. Her work has been shown at HAU and Sophiensæle.

View work →

Roman Kovács

b. 1970 Pécs (HU) · lives Budapest

Kovács works exclusively in large-format black-and-white photography, printed by hand. His ongoing project documents the disappearing rural interiors of southeastern Hungary.

View work →

Amaal Hersi

b. 1991 Mogadishu (SO) · lives London & Berlin

Hersi makes large-scale textile sculptures and wall works referencing the architectural and domestic memory of Mogadishu. She joined the gallery in 2024 and is shortlisted for the Preis der Nationalgalerie 2026.

View work →
